_about: GRADER-TYPE-1 (owner rulings R1-R2, 22 Nov 2026) LIVE probes. SYNTHETIC typed answers composed for this lane (never a student's paper). Each probe is sent on BOTH entry points (single /api/check-solution and set /api/grade-worksheet, typed transport) with acceptsV2 true. They are NOT part of the default golden plan (the G1 gate, floor.json and the stored baselines are untouched): `goldenLive.cjs --type-probes --filter T1.` plans only these, `goldenTypeProbes.cjs --run <dir>` scores them (stable = every run passes). The expectation is the OWNER RULING, written as bounds on marksLostByType (the server's own ledger) — never on prose. Papers on the `document` transport (a PDF) are not covered here: that live verify is a separate step (see the PR).

rulings.R1: HCF/LCM-type dropped power or factor: a factorisation written correctly, then used with a power/factor dropped, is `silly` ONLY when the student's own work elsewhere on the page shows the rule the use needs applied correctly; otherwise `conceptual`.
rulings.R2: Blank asked-for reason, answer right, nothing on the page proving the student knows it -> the lost mark is typed `conceptual`. With proof (knowledgeEvidence) it stays `presentation` (Exam technique).
rulings.R3: Paid golden runs include the production scheme step (the solution cache), not the null stub.

bounds: each bound is one of: 'gt0' (> 0), 'eq0' (= 0), or a number (exact). marks: [min, max] inclusive. A key left out is not checked.

probes.subject: Maths
probes.question:
(i) Write the highest power of 2 and the highest power of 3 among the numbers 1 to 10 that must divide a number that is shared equally among any 1 to 10 guests. Give a reason. [1 mark]
(ii) Hence find the least number of chocolates that can be shared equally among 1 to 10 guests. [1 mark]

probes.subject: Maths
probes.question:
(i) Write the highest power of 2 and the highest power of 3 among the numbers 1 to 10 that must divide a number that is shared equally among any 1 to 10 guests. Give a reason. [1 mark]
(ii) Hence find the least number of chocolates that can be shared equally among 1 to 10 guests. [1 mark]
probes.textAnswer:
(i) 2^3 and 3^2
(ii) LCM = product of the highest powers of the primes = 2^3 x 3^2 x 5 x 7 = 8 x 9 x 35 = 2520

probes.question: Find the LCM of 20 and 30 using prime factorisation. [2 marks]
probes.textAnswer:
20 = 2^2 x 5
30 = 2 x 3 x 5
LCM = highest powers = 2^2 x 3 x 5 = 50
